title: PR handoff & unblock playbook - Nisha
content:
Purpose:
Quick reference for how I hand off a PR when I need another reviewer to take it to merge or unblock it quickly. This is intentionally terse — copy/paste parts into PR description or Slack. Keep this doc updated with shortcuts I actually use.

Quick objective:
- Reduce friction when PR owner is offline or overloaded.
- Give reviewer a clear smallest-success path to merge (happy path) + an explicit rollback plan.

Handoff checklist (pre-handoff, what I do before tagging someone):
1) Local sanity: `make test && ./scripts/run-smoke` — green locally.
2) CI: note which CI jobs are flaky and why (list job names). If flaky, add `ci: allow-flaky` label and short note in PR.
3) PR description: top-level TL;DR (2 lines) + important context bullets: what user-visible change, which models/serving paths touched, SLO impact (latency/regression risk).
4) Files to review: include a one-line pointer for each changed module (e.g., `serving/runtime/request_router.py — routing policy change`).
5) Test signal: add 1 representative unit test name and 1 integration scenario to run locally (copy/paste).
6) Rollout plan: canary % and fallback model variant, or if not applicable, say "no rollout needed".
7) Migration notes: DB migrations (idempotent?), background jobs — list exact command to run if required.
8) Backout: how to revert quickly (branch name or revert PR link).

Tagging reviewer: what I paste in Slack/PR to request takeover:
- Short note: `@<name> small handoff: PR #4821 — fixes routing edge for multi-model fallback. Local smoke passes. CI flaky on integration-a (known). Happy path: merge + monitor logs for 10m at 99th latency. Rollback: revert PR #4821.`
- Attach links: PR, CI build, minimal runbook snippet.

If reviewer is blocked (common scenarios + scripts):
A) Block: flaky CI job (integration-a) — mitigation steps:
  - Re-run only that job (CI UI -> rerun job). If flaky again, run locally with `./tests/run_integration_a.sh` and paste failing output into PR.
  - If locally passes, post `ci: rerun-due-to-flake` and ask ops to retrigger.
B) Block: missing env secrets / infra resource only owner can create:
  - Quick workaround: add a toggle to gate the change behind `FEATURE_FLAG_TEMP` and push a minimal follow-up PR that multis the change behind the flag. Include `// TODO remove flag after infra-provision` in code.
C) Block: merge conflicts with main:
  - Rebase on main, run smoke tests, push `branch-rebased-for-merge`. If rebase causes >3 modules of diff, prefer a follow-up PR that separates concerns.

Small fix path for reviewers (what they should do to get to green asap):
1) If a single failing test, run it locally and edit test + code only if it looks like a flaky assertion (note: prefer marking flaky with `@flaky` if test infrastructure known flaky).
2) If lint/test infra error, run the formatter/linter locally: `python -m black . && tox -e lint`. Commit and push.
3) For performance regressions flagged in CI: revert the specific commit that introduced regression (use `git revert <sha>`), push a revert PR with "hotfix: revert perf regression".

Triage flow for flaky test that blocks multiple PRs:
- Collect 3 examples of failing runs (dates + CI job ids) and open a ticket (JIRA INF-FLAKY). Tag `eng-sre` and `qa` in the ticket.
- In the ticket, paste minimal repro and assignment recommendation (usually `eng-sre` owner).
- For handoff: leave note in PR `defers to JIRA-INF-FLAKY — will merge after infra fix / skip`.

PR review heuristics (my shorthand):
- Safety: any change touching request routing, auth, or storage = high-scrutiny. Ask for an SLO smoke + DB schema sketch.
- Simplicity: prefer split into two PRs if PR touches runtime + UI or runtime + infra.
- Tests: every behavioral change must have 1 unit test that covers the new branch and 1 integration scenario doc.

Slack templates (paste and tweak):
- "@<oncall> quick ask: can you help retrigger CI job `integration-a` for PR #4821? Run id: 12345. I've reproduced locally, looks flaky. Will monitor."
- "@<reviewer> small takeover request: I need to step away for 2h. PR #4821 — smoke passes, CI flaky on integration-a. If you approve, please merge and start canary at 5%. Watch logs for `request_router` errors for 10 minutes."

Follow-ups after merge (what I do within 24h):
- Watch logs for 15m across canary region(s), note any `ERROR` or sudden latency jump.
- Check platform metrics dashboard: 50th/95th/99th latency and error rate. Post quick note in the PR with screenshots.
- Open follow-up tasks for cleanup items: remove temp feature flags, tighten tests, etc.

Quick commands I actually use (copy into terminal):
- `git fetch origin && git checkout -b ~/tmp/review-4821 origin/pr/4821 && ./scripts/run-smoke`
- `gh pr checkout 4821 && gh pr review --approve --body \"LGTM — merging per handoff playbook\"`
- `kubectl logs -n prod -l app=request-router --since=10m | grep "request_router" | tail -n 200`

Open questions / notes to self:
- Should we add a small UI in Console to mark PRs as 'handoff-ready' with canned checklist? (good product ask for platform team).
- Consider a CI meta-label `flaky-flagged` that automatically pins flaky job names into PR description when re-run more than twice.

Quick wins to implement later (todo):
- Template snippets in GitHub PR description for handoffs.
- Small GH Action to add `ci: allow-flaky` label when tests retried >2x.
- Short Confluence page: "Handoff playbook (team-wide)" distilled from this doc.

Last-minute reminders (notes to self):
- Keep handoff message under 3 sentences in Slack. Reviewer attention is scarce.
- Always include rollback plan.
- If in doubt, add a small feature flag to reduce blast radius.

— end —
